launches.title: Letterpress-1: The world's first coding agent, harness, and IDE for growth engineering
launches.tagline: Letterpress-1 re-imagines every aspect of developer tooling for engineering growth.
launches.body:
Today, the Letter Company is releasing the beta of [Letterpress-1](https://letter.dev/), the world’s first coding agent, harness, and IDE purpose-built for growth engineering. We believe that growth is quickly becoming an engineering problem, but modern engineering tools aren’t designed for this type of challenge.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XD1kMTWNE9c>

Letterpress-1 is built for both the present and the future. It can set-up classic strategies like A/B testing via a _native_ interface, but also build complex tooling to sell to agents. These challenges look radically different but speak the same language: **pull requests**. 

### What makes Letterpress-1 different?

Unlike your main application, your website is reactive to the outside world. To grow quickly, you need to build on signals from various things: agents, Google ranking, customer behavior, and your competitors. Today’s leading coding agents were designed for complex codebases, but not reactiveness to external signals. 

The Letter platform and Letterpress-1 is a different type of coding agent and IDE. It can tackle challenges both tiny and massive. To illustrate this, let’s consider two examples: 

**A tiny challenge?** After installing Letterpress-1, you can directly edit content on your website itself via ⌘+L, with those edits translated into a pull-request. Stop switching between a terminal window and your website. 

**A big challenge?** You can prompt evidence chains to build conviction in external agents that your product creates real outcomes, has recurring users, and proper usage. 

### Letterpress-1 is built for today.

There are so many things that you can build with Letterpress-1 without requiring external tools. All of these are equally proactive: Letter will encourage you to build these things. For example: 

* Set-up A/B testing, and automatically prioritize winning branches based on conversion.
* Install de-anonymization via middleware, warm email addresses, and set-up outbound. 
* Find missing landing page opportunities and build them with brand consistency. 
* Detect agent behavior on LLMs.txt, [Agents.md](http://Agents.md), and all webpages. 
* Auto-triage your sitemap, flag any SEO or brand inconsistencies, and fix.

This is made possible because of Letterpress-1’s architecture. We use a mixture of state-of-the-art models, our own fine-tuned models for specific tasks (e.g. headline writing), brand evals, and built-in infrastructure for growth problems. 

When compared to Claude Code or Codex, Letterpress-1 produces better, tasteful outputs. This is made possible by orchestrating SOTA models like Claude and Codex, using fine-tuned small models for common growth tasks, and running evals to ensure brand consistency. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125321&key=user_uploads/190672/b29a32a4-95e6-4a60-93a7-6ab4bc5471bd)

However, this is just the tip of the iceberg. Letterpress-1 will also plan futuristic growth strategies to win agentic traffic and create workspaces to build them. This is made possible by Letter’s pre-built primitives, a new class of infrastructure for growth. These include: 

* Proofs, evidence chains that verify customer usage, renewals, and outcomes to build agent conviction. 
* Simulations, automatic mirror applications to enable agents to safely try solutions before committing to buying them. 
* Benches, self-hosted, reproducible benchmarks with open source, independent governance. 
* Kernels, writing pipelines to produce credible copy to appeal to agents. 
* Phantoms, automatic publications to test agentic growth strategies in a sandbox. 
* And more!

Letter makes prompting changes incredibly easy. After being installed in your build, authenticated users can prompt Letterpress-1 directly from their public web application, sharing visual brand context without manually taking a screenshot.
